title: Skip the certified-commit ancestry test on a shallow clone
summary: The unit check failed on the first CI run of this branch. test_certified_commit_is_on_this_branch asks git whether the certified commit of configs/approved_code_version.json is an ancestor of HEAD, and it skipped only when that commit was absent. CI clones at depth 1 with a blob filter; git fetches the commit on demand there, so the test did not skip, and the ancestry question failed because the clone holds no history. A fresh shallow partial clone of the branch reproduces it: cat-file exits 0 and merge-base --is-ancestor exits 1. With the program lead's approval the test now also skips when git reports a shallow repository. It still runs on full clones, where it passes. CI no longer checks ancestry.
next: Merge after green CI, then post the issue rewrites.
reason: One test gains a skip condition for shallow clones. No result, gate value or owner file changes.
